short: A blunt career soldier who ended a year of civil war and rebuilt imperial finances on solid, unglamorous footing.
full:
Vespasian, commanding the war against the Jewish revolt, was proclaimed emperor by the legions of Egypt and Judaea on 1 July 69 CE, the date he later reckoned as the start of his reign. After his forces defeated Vitellius, the Senate confirmed him that December, ending the civil war that had followed Nero's death and founding the Flavian dynasty.

A provincial equestrian family with no link to the old aristocracy, the Flavians governed pragmatically: Vespasian restored the treasury through new taxes, expanded the Senate with provincial families, and began construction of the Colosseum on the site of Nero's private lake. He died of illness on 23 June 79 CE, reportedly joking on his deathbed that he was becoming a god, and was succeeded smoothly by his elder son Titus.
